purpose: Edit multiline plain text with native text editing, form submission and validation semantics.
avoid: Do not infer validation limits from sample content.
basis: Pinned React/primitive sources lead API, lifecycle and semantics; native visual observations and explicit reference decisions are mapped in figma/traceability.json.
profileRationale: The family presents controls or navigation; static depictions do not establish an interactive contract.
sourceRule: The wrapper is exactly a native textarea with React.ComponentProps<textarea>. value/defaultValue, name, required, disabled, readOnly, maxLength, rows and onChange are native props. It adds field-sizing-content and a minimum height, not autosave, rich text, a submit-on-Enter handler or a new value callback.
keyboardAndFocus: Native multiline editing and IME apply. Enter inserts a newline, Tab leaves the control, Escape does not revert committed text. Disabled suppresses editing and native form submission; readOnly permits focus/copy and retains its submitted value. Caller owns validation and explicit error relations.
contentAlternative: Visible native labels, destinations and task text provide the meaning; icons, borders and position are supplementary.

referenceDecision: Concrete labels, destination fragments and validation text are caller-supplied examples. The bound source wrapper does not automatically supply those application decisions.

visualContract.layoutPolicy: Textarea is the actual native textarea export. Native 64px minimum height, 8/10px padding and 10px corners become semantic roles; the 360px sample width does not become a runtime constraint. Source field-sizing-content is represented directly, with a minimum-height fallback and native vertical resizing. Content can grow instead of clipping to a specimen height. Native label/help/error IDs are caller decisions, while readOnly, disabled, multiline value/selection/IME and native events remain browser-owned. Readonly stays focusable and selectable; disabled prevents user edits and is skipped in Tab order. Invalid styling supplements a linked readable error and does not invent validation.
